worst_places.quote: Четыре правила по убыванию приоритета: (1) `new` — `this` = новый объект; (2) explicit binding (`call`/`apply`/`bind`) — `this` = первый аргумент; (3) implicit binding (вызов через объект `obj.fn()`) — `this` = объект слева от точки; (4) default binding (самостоятельный вызов) — `this` = `globalThis` в sloppy mode или `undefined` в strict mode.

worst_places.before: Четыре правила по убыванию приоритета: (1) `new` — `this` = новый объект; (2) explicit binding (`call`/`apply`/`bind`) — `this` = первый аргумент; (3) implicit binding (вызов через объект `obj.fn()`) — `this` = объект слева от точки; (4) default binding (самостоятельный вызов) — `this` = `globalThis` в sloppy mode или `undefined` в strict mode.
worst_places.after:
Правил четыре, приоритет — сверху вниз:

```txt
new Fn()          → this = новый объект
fn.call/apply/bind → this = первый аргумент
obj.fn()          → this = объект слева от точки
fn()              → this = globalThis (sloppy) / undefined (strict)
```

Если подходят сразу два правила, побеждает то, что выше.

worst_places.after: `class` is syntactic sugar over the prototype mechanism. There are three real differences from a manual constructor. First, class methods are non-enumerable, as if defined with `Object.defineProperty` and `enumerable: false`; a manual `prototype.method = fn` is enumerable. Second, calling a class without `new` throws a `TypeError`; a constructor function just runs as a normal call. Third, `extends` sets up two chains, not one: `Derived.prototype[[Prototype]] = Base.prototype` for instances, and `Derived[[Prototype]] = Base` for static methods.

patterns: POSITIVE — the house structure of articles 01-12 is the best on the site and should be lifted verbatim into the style guide: (1) every section opens with a one-sentence plain claim and no warm-up («Замыкание = функция + ссылка на Environment Record», «`this` — это не переменная»), (2) a ```txt ASCII diagram or a numbered spec algorithm comes within 2-3 lines of the claim, before any second idea, (3) a runnable code block with the expected value written as an inline `// comment` on the same line follows immediately, (4) each article ends with the same two fixed sections — «Связь с другими темами» (a txt block of cross-links) and «Типичные ошибки на интервью» (quoted myth → нет/no → correction). The result is that theory never runs more than ~4 sentences before an example, which is why D and E average 4.8 here versus much lower in other zones.

POSITIVE — the myth-first bullet («"Хойстинг поднимает код наверх"» — код не перемещается…) is the single most reusable device in the zone: it states what the reader probably believes, refutes it in one word, then gives the mechanism. It appears 6-7 times per article and is why C averages 4.8. Two conditions make it work and must be written into the guide: the quoted claim must be FALSE (ru/07 breaks this and answers «да»), and the refutation must be the second or third word, not buried.

POSITIVE — abbreviations that ARE expanded are expanded by structure, not by parenthesis: the spec term gets its own H2/H3 in full («Temporal Dead Zone — что реально происходит», «Environment Records — что за ними стоит») and the short form is used only afterwards. The failures listed in unexpanded_abbrevs are almost all cases where the short form leaked into an earlier file section or into an ASCII diagram before that heading arrived (TDZ at line 46 of article 01, GC in the article 09 lifecycle diagram).

NEGATIVE — the RU locale is the second-class citizen wherever the two versions diverged. Every divergence found goes the same direction: EN fixed, RU stale. ru/07 keeps the broken myth bullet EN repaired; ru/08 keeps the `createLogger` example that references a variable declared later, which EN rewrote; ru/12 names a variable `byLength` while grouping by parity, which EN renamed to `byParity`; ru/13 prints «Ответ: `3, 1, 4, 2`» in the open where en/13 hides every answer in `<details><summary>Answer</summary>`, so the RU self-test is spoiled before it is attempted. RU also carries four garbled words that no proofreader saw («Семь простанство», «трансп», «полупривате», «Оrinoco» with a Cyrillic О).

NEGATIVE — the quiz bank was clearly authored separately from the articles and never reconciled with them: it says `var` has a TDZ (article 01 says the opposite in bold), it puts Rendering after Macrotasks (article 05's diagram puts it between them), and RU uses the transliterations «Микротаски/Макротаски» where all thirteen RU articles use «микрозадачи/макрозадачи». The bank also refers to distractors by index («Вариант 2», «Option 0», «Option B») in three mutually incompatible schemes, none of which the reader can see on screen. The articles never do this.
